answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonded escrows that make coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities produce mutually corroborating conflicting votes, pairwise evidence grows as O(k²), so aggregate penalties scale quadratically rather than per identity alone. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss across the controlled swarm, making identity splitting uneconomic. The dawn-to-ridge audit trail can expose the mirror pattern of shared equivocation without treating ordinary correlated behavior as proof.
